report_html:
A Ground-First Machine

Their backs are a real part of the passing game — RBs see 25% of targets (vs ~18%), which props up the back's reception floor.

The Offensive Blueprint

They're a heavy under-center team (57% shotgun vs ~68%) — a pro-style, run-committed structure.

When they fall behind they abandon the run entirely — 58% pass while trailing, so their pass-catchers have huge comeback-script ceilings.

By the numbers it's an efficient unit — a 47% success rate (above the 44% average).

In the Red Zone

Their red-zone identity is run-first (50% pass), funnelling touchdown equity to the lead back.

Defense — No Obvious Seam

They lock down opposing WR1s — just 51 rec yds/game (vs ~58); fade receiving props there.

They lock down opposing WR2s — just 30 rec yds/game (vs ~36); fade receiving props there.

They leak RB rushing TDs (0.67/game vs ~0.46) — an anytime-TD spot to attack.

They surrender 119 rushing and 219 passing yards per game (league ~120 / ~230). No dominant funnel — read it matchup by matchup.

Broadly a leaky unit — 47% success rate allowed (vs ~44%); points come easy against them.

They leak TE touchdowns (0.31/game vs ~0.24) — an anytime-TD spot to attack.

The Betting Angles

Bottom line: back their RB1's rushing volume in favored/positive scripts; their pass-catchers have massive ceilings in comeback scripts (fade-material as underdogs); opposing TE anytime-TD is a repeatable angle.

Built on 2024–25 data; the profile rebuilds through the season as the current staff and roster set their own tendencies.
